To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the bonding strength is determined by the atomic bond strength, (ii) the interface strength can be improved by reducing the interface void fraction, (iii) notches caused by the etching step prior to bonding reduce the fracture limit, (iv) stress corrosion effects reduce the bonding strength of stressed components, (v) the time-to-fail data can be theoretically predicted by a fracture mechanics approach.
the fracture strength of wafer-bonds is determined by the interface strength, the interface quality, the notch size, the loading rate, the loading time, and the temperature.
the strength of wafer-bonds is mainly limited by interface voids and that the lifetime of wafer-bounded sensors and actuators is mainly determined by the stress corrosion of the interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new micromachining process for the fabrication of micromechanic components with wafer-bonding technology.
the strength and reliability assessment of micrometer-sized mechanical structures which are fabricated by wafer-bonding technologies.
the mechanical characterization and reliability of wafer-bonds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

wafer bonding can be considered a very promising technique for the fabrication of micromechans components, if the bonding strength and the stress corrosion effects are taken into account in the design and the reliability assessment.

the mechanical reliability assessment of micromechnical sensors and actuators is a very complex task and needs to be performed by the manufacturer in the development stage as well as by the user in the application stage.

the wafer bonding technique is a reliable method for the fabrication of micromechancial sensors and actuators if the bonding interfaces are protected against the mechanical load during the application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fracture mechanics approach is an appropriate tool for the strength and reliability assessment of waferred wafer-bonding technologies.
wafer bonding is an attractive technology for micromechanical applications if the fracture strength and the reliability are considered in an appropriate manner.
wafer-bonding technologies can be applied to fabricate micromechanical structures with sufficient strength and mechanical reliability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fracture strength of wafer-bonds is not limited by the bonding strength, but rather by stress corrosion effects which decrease the bonding strength with time.
the mechanical reliability of wafer-bonds can be significantly improved by a reduction of the interface voids.
the fracture limit and lifetime of wafer-boned components depend not only on the mechanical loading but also on the bonding strength and the stress corrosion sensitivity.
